headline: Ward 21 ranks 34th of 50 wards, strongest on school funding and street repair.
summary:
Ward 21 covers Washington Heights, West Pullman, Morgan Park, and Roseland on Chicago's Far South Side. It ranks 34th out of 50 wards overall, with a combined score of 37.04. Most of what's measured here comes with a caveat attached, 164 of the 181 rankings that exist for this ward.

The strongest numbers cluster around schools and streets. Per-pupil school spending ranks 2nd of 50, and just over 97 percent of the ward's aldermanic menu money went to resurfacing streets, itself a top-3 citywide share. The weak spots sit on the retail and nightlife side. Ward 21 has the highest share of chain restaurants of any ward, no bars rated 4.5 stars or higher with at least 50 reviews, and almost no restaurants licensed to serve liquor. That combination describes a residential ward where schools and street paving are the visible public investment, not a built-out commercial strip.
reading_the_rankings: Three of Ward 21's six best rankings measure religious attendance, and all three come from the same model, not a survey taken here. The weekly-attendance and strongly-religious figures are built from national survey patterns matched to the ward's demographics, and the source itself rates the estimate low confidence, so read them as what a ward with this population mix tends to look like rather than a count of who is in a pew on Sunday. The alley-repair and spending-diversity rankings near the bottom are really the flip side of the street-paving strength. With 97 percent of menu money going to streets, there was almost nothing left over for alleys or any other category, which is why both land in the mid-40s out of 50. And the liquor-license ranking, 49th of 50, looks worse than the gap behind it. Twelve other wards score within two points of Ward 21 on that measure, so the real distance between near-last and the middle of the pack is thin.

news.headline: South Siders Still Waiting For Tree Cleanup After June Storms, But City Departments Are Overwhelmed
news.note: June storms left about 1,600 tree-related 311 requests open in Ward 21, the second-highest count of any ward, with hundreds still unresolved three weeks later.

news.headline: City program to rehab more than 30 properties on the South and West sides is back
news.note: Rebuild Chicago 2.0 is using a $20 million state grant to rehab and resell 33 vacant homes in Roseland and Englewood.
